Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The players are back out in the middle. Tanzid Hasan and Parvez Hossain Emon are the openers for Bangladesh. Asitha Fernando will start off proceedings with the first new ball, to Parvez. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, with the average total at this venue hovering around 260, Sri Lanka do look about 10-15 runs short. That said, this pitch hasn’t been the easiest to bat on, especially for new batters, and the hosts will be hoping to make the most of the home conditions. Bangladesh, on the other hand, would have gladly accepted this target at the start, and with the possibility of dew setting in, they'll be quietly confident about chasing it down, provided they get off to a solid start. No matter how it unfolds, we’re in for an exciting second half. Stay tuned as we get ready for the chase!

Bangladesh will feel they left a bit on the table, but overall, they'll be satisfied with their bowling display. Taskin Ahmed set things in motion with two early strikes, while Tanzim Hasan Sakib delivered a big blow by dismissing the in-form Nissanka for a duck. Although they went through a quiet phase in the middle, debutant Tanvir Islam provided a much-needed breakthrough by breaking a threatening stand. Despite a couple of bowlers struggling with cramps and being unable to dislodge the determined Asalanka, they kept chipping away from the other end. Taskin finished with an impressive four-wicket haul, Tanzim grabbed three, and Najmul Hossain Shanto chipped in with one before Tawhid Hridoy capped off the innings with a run out.

Sri Lanka found themselves in early trouble, but steady and composed batting from skipper Charith Asalanka and Kusal Mendis helped them recover. The duo stitched together a crucial 60-run partnership before Mendis fell short of a deserved half-century. The captain then built another solid stand with debutant Milan Rathnayake, steering the hosts into a strong position to post a competitive total. Wanindu Hasaranga chipped in with a handy cameo, but the lower order couldn't offer much resistance, and they failed to capialise in the last ten overs. Still, Asalanka held firm with a gritty century and guided his side to a fighting total just shy of 250.

That brings an end to a rollercoaster first half of the match! All eyes will be on Sri Lankan skipper Charith Asalanka, who notched up his fifth ODI century and once again led from the front to rescue his side from a tricky position. But credit must also go to Bangladesh's bowlers, while they lost their way a bit during the middle phase, they started strong and finished well to keep things evenly poised heading into the second innings.

Asitha then turns around and calls his partner through for the second on the overthrow. But Tawhid Hridoy charges in from square leg and stops the ball before it can go to the deep. Picks the ball up and fires a throw at the bowler's end, to catch Eshan Malinga well short. SRI LANKA HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 244!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. Good passage of play for the hosts. The last 5 overs have gone for 29 without much risks being taken. This partnership itself, between Asalanka and Liyanage is going well, at 45 (54). Bangladesh are trying to stall the run flow, but every now and then, have tended to slip in a loose ball. In addition, the heat is not making things easy and despite coming from Bangladesh, where the heat is more or less the same, they are struggling with their fitness levels. Sri Lanka look good to get a score in excess of 260 from here on, but it will be interesting to see how the new rule of using only one ball post the 34th over affects this game. Asalanka is playing yet one of those innings, taking his team from recovery to dominance. Not much batting left after this pair though, so the visitors will look to break this stand and then run through the lower middle order. Meanwhile, Mustafizur Rahman returns. 4-1-15-0 so far.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. It is a hot day in Colombo and the water break has come early. Good cat-and-mouse cricket going on, with Bangladesh starting well with the ball but Sri Lanka fighting back with a quickfire partnership. Both, Kusal Mendis and Charith Asalanka have looked positive from the get go. Sri Lanka lost three wickets inside the 7th over but some proactiveness from first, Kusal and then, skipper Asalanka, has kept the scoreboard ticking at a decent pace. Else, it is very easy to get bogged down when wickets fall in a heap. It could also be a case of the pitch getting batter to bat on, after the early moisture on the wicket evaporated. However, this partnership is the key for Lankans. Given the heat, there is a big chance of expecting turn around the 25th-30th over and post the 34th over, since we will be having only one ball, reverse swing could come into play as well, given the abrasiveness of the surface. So it really is going to be an exciting match to watch out for. Bangladesh have been on the money more or less and even though skipper Mehidy has been taken for some reasons, expect him to bounce back soon.

Commentary.Commentary: Good observation by Russel Arnold on air. He sees a few bowling lines marked around the bowler's release point. Normally, such markings are seen around the starting runup of the bowlers. But maybe, because bowlers are overstepping, they want an extra information about the point from where they are about to release the ball, so that they can keep the foot behind the line. Interesting.

Commentary.Commentary: The Bangladesh players get into a last-minute huddle. Out walk the Lakan openers - Pathum Nissanka - boy, Bangladesh must have got used to seeing him almost every day. In a Test series that spanned over 9 days, Nissanka must have batted for at least 4 days. He has got a new opening partner in Nishan Madushka. As expected, Taskin Ahmed will take the first new ball. Remember, the rules are changed from this series. We shall have two new balls till the 34th over and from the 35th, we shall have only one for the rest of the innings. All set then, Nissanka to face.

The national anthems are done and dusted and we are all set for the ODI series to kick off. A few paras below, you might have read about rain projected to play a part in this game. But for now, the conditions are bright and sunny, and extremely hot. Dew could be a factor in the run chase and at the same time, rain could make things easier on DLS for the side batting second. But looking at this heat, it is pretty logical to bat first, because if it does not rain, the odd ball might stay low in the second innings.

We are moments away from the start of the game, but before that, the players from both sides make their way out and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first, followed by the national anthem of Sri Lanka.

PITCH REPORT - Farveez Maharoof is pitchside. He starts by saying that it’s hot and humid out there, and conditions will definitely test the players physically. Adds that the pitch looks like a good one for ODI cricket and should hold up well throughout the 100 overs. Mentions that the surface is quite hard on top, with a neat layer of brown grass that has been rolled in well, giving it a smooth finish. States that batting early on, especially against the new ball, will be relatively comfortable with the ball coming nicely onto the bat. Further adds that once the ball gets older, the surface may slow down a touch, and that’s when spinners will start to have more of a say in the game. Talks about how the pitch offers something for everyone and feels that a total in the range of 260 to 280 could prove to be a match-winning score on this surface.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz, the captain of Bangladesh, says that they have two debutants. Adds that Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanvir Islam have been waiting for a long time to get into the team. Adds that the wicket looks good, but dew will be a factor, as they saw that when they practiced last night. Mentions that it is going to be a challenge for them in these conditions, but they have prepared well and are confident going into this game.

Charith Asalanka, the skipper of Sri Lanka says that the wicket looks decent to bat on and will want to put runs on the board up front. Informs that Milan Rathnayake is making his debut. He comes in for Dunith Wellalage from the last game. Mentions that they have gone with two seamers in the playing XI, as dew can play a factor in the second inning.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon (On Debut), Najmul Hossain Shanto, Litton Das (WK), Tawhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali, Mehidy Hasan Miraz (C), Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Tanvir Islam (On Debut) and Tanzim Hasan Sakib.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Nishan Madushka, Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kamindu Mendis, Charith Asalanka (C), Janith Liyanage, Milan Rathnayake (On Debut), Wanindu Hasaranga, Maheesh Theekshana, Eshan Malinga and Asitha Fernando.

Just in - The update from the Sri Lankan camp is that Milan Rathnayake has received his maiden ODI cap and will be making his debut in this match. Meanwhile, Bangladesh have two debutants of their own - Tanvir Islam and Parvez Hossain Emon, both set to feature in their first ODI.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of Charith Asalanka. Sri Lanka have won the toss and elected to BAT first.

As for the conditions, Colombo might offer a spin-heavy challenge, and the clouds are hovering over the ground. There are chances of rain, but hopefully it stays away. The toss could play a big role in shaping the game plan, and chasing under lights might be easier. All in all, a tight contest is on the cards for all of us. With that, stay tuned for the toss and playing XI!

Bangladesh, meanwhile, are in the middle of a rebuild, as their experienced players like Mushfiqur Rahim and Mahmudullah have taken retirement from ODIs. Mehidy Hasan Miraz takes charge of a young squad that’s searching for consistency and a spark to light their new era. Litton Das, Najmul Hossain Shanto, and Tawhid Hridoy will be crucial with the bat, while Mustafizur Rahman and Taskin Ahmed will be key with the ball. Their recent disappointment in the Champions Trophy still lingers, and this series presents an opportunity to bounce back, test new combinations, and build a stronger core for the preparations of the 2027 ODI World Cup. Although the Tigers may be underdogs on paper, they’ve got bite to challenge the Lankans.

Sri Lanka come into the series with confidence and home advantage, eager to bounce back in the ODI circuit after failing to qualify for the 2025 Champions Trophy. They have played well, especially in the longest format, Tests, where they were even in contention to reach the final in the last concluded WTC, but unfortunately, missed out in the end. In the last three years or so, they have built a core that looks pretty solid. The trio of Wanindu Hasaranga, Maheesh Theekshana, and Dunith Wellalage promises spin mayhem, while Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis, and skipper Charith Asalanka will carry the batting load. Their pace unit also looks sharp, offering a well-rounded attack ready to strike. This team looks like a well-balanced side, hungry for the win.

Hello and welcome to the first ODI between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, which is set to be played at the R. Premadasa Stadium, Colombo. Sri Lanka won the recently concluded Test series by 1-0, and while the result didn't go in favour of Bangladesh, they have played good cricket. Now, the focus shifts to the white-ball format as the ODI series begins.
... MATCH DAY ...

After just a three-day break, that too because the last Test ended on the fourth day, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka are back at it again, this time switching from red-ball to white-ball cricket as the ODI leg of the tour kicks off. That’s the modern rhythm of international cricket - fast-paced, relentless, and driven by both the demands of broadcasters and the hunger of fans for non-stop action. From spinning tracks to fast outfields, players now juggle formats within days, often with little time to rest or reset. And now, the battle will resume at the iconic R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo, where two proud cricketing nations reignite a growing rivalry that’s fast becoming one of Asia’s most watchable contests. A lion vs tiger fight, as fans like to call it, Sri Lanka vs Bangladesh. Both teams have many things on the line. Though Sri Lanka sit at No. 4 in the ICC ODI rankings and Bangladesh at No. 10, the gap on paper doesn't reflect how intense these games can be. When Sri Lanka last toured Bangladesh, it was the Tigers who came out on top in the ODIs with a 2-1 series win. Now, in their own den, Sri Lanka will be eager to restore pride, while Bangladesh look to punch above their weight and build a unit for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Stakes? Sky high. Sri Lanka, fresh off a 1-0 series win in Tests, will aim to carry forward that momentum into their favourite format. The island nation has always cherished their ODI history, World Cup winners, Asia Cup champions, and a side that always thrives in home conditions. Their recent white-ball form has been solid in the last year or so, with notable series wins against teams like India and Australia, and now they want to keep their heads high after missing out on the Champions Trophy 2025, as they failed to get in the top eight after the end of the last World Cup 2023 league phase. Leading the charge is Pathum Nissanka, who was outstanding in the Tests with back-to-back hundreds, and will now look to fix his numbers in ODIs this year, as he has been their best batter in the last three years in this format. Kusal Mendis, alongside skipper Charith Asalanka and the ever-promising Kamindu Mendis, gives this side a middle-order that knows how to soak pressure. There’s also a possible return for Sadeera Samarawickrama in the playing XI, who could add more firepower. But where Sri Lanka look truly dangerous is their spin trio, Wanindu Hasaranga, Maheesh Theekshana, and Dunith Wellalage, three world-class spinners who can torment any batting order on turning tracks in white-ball cricket. They’re supported by a returning Dilshan Madushanka, who adds bite to the pace attack, which already includes Asitha Fernando and Eshan Malinga. The squad is youthful but experienced enough, and above all, hungry to rise again in ODI cricket. Bangladesh, meanwhile, are at a crucial transition phase. With some senior players stepping away, a fresh chapter begins under the leadership of Mehidy Hasan Miraz, who now has the responsibility to guide this team forward. Their Champions Trophy campaign earlier this year didn’t go as planned, and questions have loomed over the side’s form and approach in big tournaments. But in Mehidy, the board sees a calm thinker and a cricketer who leads by example. At the top, Litton Das and Mohammad Naim are likely to open, tasked with giving solid starts. Just behind them is Najmul Hossain Shanto at number three, who has been Bangladesh’s most consistent batter in recent years. After stepping down from captaincy in the Test format just a couple of days ago, he’ll now aim to bat with freedom, as he indicated. In the middle order, Tawhid Hridoy and Jaker Ali represent a new generation, and this series could be the perfect stage for them to rise. In the bowling department, Taskin Ahmed remains the leader of the pace attack, with Nahid Rana offering youth and fire, while Mustafizur Rahman, with all his tricks and experience, will be expected to deliver at the death. The biggest question mark lies in their spin unit, as Mehidy himself is the frontline spinner, but hasn’t been consistently threatening. For Bangladesh to win here, they’ll need not just leadership, but collective fire, with bat and ball. Talking about the conditions, Colombo has traditionally been spin-friendly, especially under lights. The last ODI series played here against Australia saw Sri Lanka’s spinners choke their opposition with sharp turn and bounce. Expect the same script to unfold, especially with players like Hasaranga and Theekshana in the mix. Batters from both sides will be tested thoroughly. The toss could be a crucial factor, as there’s rain predicted in the morning, and a delayed start could make chasing a smarter option. Still, with both teams having plenty to prove, fans should brace themselves for a gripping contest filled with nerves, skill, and surprises. Will Sri Lanka assert their dominance at home? Or will Bangladesh roar back with purpose? We’re all set for a cracker!
